llm.summary: The skill mainly performs pre-bid analysis, but it also handles account registration, device fingerprinting, plaintext API key storage, and active HTML report generation in ways users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses vendor API calls and says registration requires consent, but automatic registration collects and transmits platform, CPU architecture, and a deterministic MAC-address hash, which is a stable device identifier beyond ordinary bid analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install script or dependency installer was found, and metadata only declares ZLBX_API_KEY; the skill separately documents local file reads, report writes, network calls, and credential storage inside runtime instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is broad for pre-bid and project-background requests, complete mode defaults to creating an HTML file, and report/output instructions require vendor links and next-step referrals rather than keeping all commercial content optional.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a reusable API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes HTML reports under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/; the credential flow lacks documented permission hardening, and the HTML renderer inserts unvalidated URL values into active reports.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core bid-analysis workflow is coherent with the stated purpose, but the skill expands into automatic account provisioning, recharge-link generation, and vendor cross-promotion; these are related to using the vendor API but broader than analysis itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you are uncomfortable with automatic vendor account creation, transmission of a hashed MAC address, storing an API key in a local JSON file, or creating shareable HTML reports with vendor links. Prefer setting your own ZLBX_API_KEY manually to avoid auto-registration, and treat generated HTML reports as active browser files rather than neutral plain documents.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local reading of user-provided bid files and writing reports are expected for this purpose and are disclosed in SKILL.md, but they are not reflected in explicit metadata permissions.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic registration and recharge-link handling support vendor API access, but collecting a stable MAC hash and persisting account credentials materially expands the skill beyond simple pre-bid analysis.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The account provisioning and monetization workflow is documented rather than hidden, but it is a separate security/privacy function embedded inside a procurement-analysis skill.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The mandatory trigger covers broad project-background and pre-bid requests, which can route users into paid API-backed workflows when a lighter or offline answer might have sufficed.
[SQP-2] expected: HTML export is aligned with report sharing, but complete mode defaults to writing a local file and disclosing the absolute path without a separate opt-in at export time.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese output is consistent with the Chinese-language skill and market context; this is a usability limitation, not a security concern by itself.
[E1] unexpected: The external transmission is disclosed and consent-gated, but the transmitted MAC hash remains a persistent pseudonymous device identifier.
[T01] unexpected: The artifact requires vendor recommendations and hard-coded promotional links in generated reports; this affects neutrality but does not show system compromise.
[T05] unexpected: The MAC-hash registration flow is artifact-backed and proportionally concerning because it accesses a stable hardware-derived identifier for account deduplication.
[T09] unexpected: The renderer uses escaping that is not safe for quoted href attributes and does not validate URL schemes, so API-returned or user-supplied links can affect generated HTML reports; the plaintext API key storage concern is also artifact-backed.
